For the second year in a row, WE Applied Technology Schools continue to demonstrate their leadership in innovation and entrepreneurship, after winning first place in the national Startup Teen competition for entrepreneurship and technological innovation, organized by iSchool.
The competition featured robust representation from WE Schools spanning eight governorates, with 79 students putting forward 19 innovative projects. Out of 102 teams competing nationwide, nine teams advanced to the semi-finals. Two teams ultimately reached the final round, accounting for one-third of all national finalists.
The WE Schools team from Alexandria Governorate won first place for their project “Basita,” an application designed to streamline home maintenance and finishing services. By directly connecting consumers with verified technicians and suppliers, the platform enhances service reliability and price transparency.
Commenting on the achievement, Eng. Tamer El Mahdi, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt, stated that the victory highlights the impact of the company's strategy to invest in youth capabilities, and build a generation that possesses technical skills, a spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship, capable of transforming ideas into real solutions and promising projects that contribute to supporting the Egyptian digital economy and achieving sustainable development.
Telecom Egypt, the total telecom operator in Egypt and one of the largest subsea cable operators in the region, has announced the signing of an agreement to construct the Sharm El Sheikh–Taba subsea cable in accordance with the company’s new strategy. The new cable will extend Telecom Egypt’s Red Sea Subsea Festoon Cable System to Taba, creating a continuous subsea connectivity path linking Suez, Zafarana, Ras Ghareb, Sharm El Sheikh, and Taba. The project marks a key milestone in expanding the Company’s subsea infrastructure across the Red Sea and Sinai, further strengthening Egypt’s position as a strategic global connectivity hub.
The Sharm El Sheikh–Taba subsea link is a vital step forward toward completing connectivity between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, by connecting onward through the Internet Corridor of Egypt (ICE). The approximately 200-kilometer, repeaterless, high-fiber-count submarine cable is designed to provide one of the shortest, fastest, and most secure connectivity routes between Sharm El Sheikh and Taba, with a design capacity of approximately five petabits per second. Using the latest fiber-optic technology, the link will deliver lower signal losses, enhanced network performance, and greater capacity, while providing international carriers and network operators with increased route diversity and connectivity options. The system is expected to be ready for service in the fourth quarter of 2027.
The extended Red Sea Subsea Festoon Cable System will further strengthen Telecom Egypt’s Red Sea infrastructure by adding new landing-point options and an additional subsea path along the coastline. This will enhance network resilience and redundancy, and provide greater routing flexibility for international traffic transiting Egypt between Asia, Africa, and Europe.
The agreement was signed in Cairo by Tamer El Mahdi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Telecom Egypt, and Byron Skaftouros, Managing Director of Power Sub Link (PSL), in the presence of H.E. Raafat Hendy, Minister of Communications and Information Technology.
Under the agreement, PSL, a global leader in advanced subsea installation and marine engineering technologies, will implement the Sharm El Sheikh–Taba subsea cable.
H.E. Raafat Hendy, Minister of Communications and Information Technology, commented:
“This agreement reflects Egypt’s continued efforts to strengthen its digital infrastructure and enhance the diversity and resilience of its international connectivity routes and reinforce Egypt's pivotal role in global digital connectivity. The development of the new subsea cable further reinforces the role of Sinai as an important component of Egypt’s digital infrastructure by expanding its subsea and terrestrial infrastructure. The Ministry is committed to strengthening Egypt’s position as a global connectivity hub between East and West, and to continuing the development of its international digital infrastructure to support global data traffic and meet the growing demand for secure, efficient, and diverse international data transmission.”
Tamer El Mahdi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Telecom Egypt, commented:
“This project aligns with our new strategy, which aims to maximize the Company's role in digital infrastructure and strengthen its position regionally and internationally. The Sharm-Taba cable is another significant milestone in the development of Telecom Egypt’s international infrastructure, particularly its subsea infrastructure in Sinai, strengthening route diversity, resilience, and capacity. It advances a new eastern digital corridor connecting the Red Sea and the Mediterranean through the Sinai Peninsula, reinforcing our strategy of leveraging Egypt’s unique geographic position at the crossroads of three continents. These investments demonstrate Telecom Egypt’s continued commitment to supporting our international partners with secure, resilient, and high-capacity connectivity routes to meet the region’s growing data demand.”
Byron Skaftouros, Managing Director of Power Sub Link, commented:
“Together with Telecom Egypt, we are not simply delivering subsea infrastructure; we are helping shape the next generation of global connectivity. By developing a resilient Red Sea bypass, we reinforce Egypt’s position as a strategic gateway between continents, strengthen the security and continuity of international communications, and create new digital corridors of lasting global significance. This is more than connectivity. It is resilience, strategic relevance, and infrastructure built for the future.”
Telecom Egypt (WE), the nation's first integrated telecom operator, has entered into a strategic partnership with City Edge Developments to deliver Triple Play services and advanced digital solutions to customers and residents of several of its flagship projects in New Alamein City, including The Gate Towers, North Edge Towers, and Mazarine Compound.
This collaboration aligns with Telecom Egypt's strategy to expand its support for the digital infrastructure of new urban communities and enhance their readiness for digital transformation. The agreement was signed by Eng. Tamer El Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt, and Eng. Tamer Nasser, CEO of City Edge Developments.
Pursuant to the agreement, WE will deploy a comprehensive suite of Triple Play services—comprising high-speed fiber-optic internet, high-definition IPTV, and fixed-line services—ensuring residents receive reliable, high-performance connectivity that meets the highest standards of quality and efficiency. This initiative directly supports City Edge Developments' strategic vision to construct smart, sustainable urban communities powered by next-generation digital infrastructure, thereby elevating the overall living experience, connectivity, and quality of life for its residents.
This strategic partnership underscores a mutual commitment to advancing technology adoption and expanding robust digital infrastructure across emerging urban developments. It also supports the Egyptian government's drive towards digital transformation and the deployment of smart, sustainable cities. By seamlessly integrating essential digital communications into the core infrastructure, the collaboration ensures an elevated living experience tailored to the evolving needs of both year-round residents and seasonal visitors.
It is worth noting that This agreement aligns with City Edge Developments' broader strategy to forge alliances with industry-leading organizations, leveraging specialized technical expertise and technological capabilities to deliver high-value services across its portfolio.
Additionally, this initiative reinforces the status of The Gate Towers, North Edge Towers, and Mazarine Compound as premier, fully integrated urban destinations within New Alamein City. By pairing world-class architectural design with advanced digital infrastructure, City Edge offers a comprehensive living experience tailored to the evolving aspirations and future requirements of its residents.
In a strategic effort to advance digital transformation within higher education, Telecom Egypt and Ain Shams University have entered into a joint cooperation agreement signed at the historic Zaafaran Palace. Under this protocol, the university will deploy and operate the "WE SmartED" solution—an AI-driven educational technology framework powered by Telecom Egypt's Digital SmartED platform to optimize academic and administrative workflows.
This milestone confirms that Telecom Egypt has met all eligibility criteria to join this segment. Driven by the stock reaching new highs, the Company’s market capitalization rose to approximately USD 3.9 billion, clearing the minimum threshold required for Mid Cap inclusion by a wide margin.
The project's initial phase will serve approximately 10,000 students and faculty members during the current academic year. The agreement was executed by Eng. Tamer El Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt, and Prof. Dr. Mohamed Diaa Zein El Abdeen, President of Ain Shams University. Under the terms of the agreement, the platform will be deployed across the university as a one-year pilot program.
Furthermore, moving into the Mid Cap segment strengthens Telecom Egypt’s appeal as an investment opportunity, enabling it to leverage inflows from index-tracking international funds. This change may support trading volumes, the Company’s visibility, and its credibility among global institutional investors.
This initiative aims to advance digital transformation and modernize the educational ecosystem by leveraging cutting-edge technology. By equipping students and faculty members with smart digital tools, the platform addresses learning gaps and drives academic excellence. Additionally, advanced analytics will track student performance, monitor engagement, and enable specialized technical and operational teams to assess operational quality for continuous institutional improvement.
“The solution is designed to build an integrated, efficient digital learning ecosystem by leveraging modern technology to enhance interaction and streamline access to educational content, ultimately delivering a more advanced and sustainable academic experience.”
The project delivers end-to-end technical and operational support to ensure seamless adoption, with phase one targeting select colleges and coursework. This initiative is positioned to elevate educational outcomes, boost academic engagement, and establish a model for AI integration across Egyptian higher education.
Telecom Egypt announced its inclusion in the FTSE Emerging Markets Index following its upgrade within the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (GEIS) from the Small Cap to the Mid Cap segment, as part of the index provider’s semi-annual review for September 2026 for the Middle East and Africa region.
This milestone confirms that Telecom Egypt has met all eligibility criteria to join this segment. Driven by the stock reaching new highs, the Company’s market capitalization rose to approximately USD 3.9 billion, clearing the minimum threshold required for Mid Cap inclusion by a wide margin.
The transition clearly reflects improved liquidity, stronger cash flows, and robust financial and operational performance. It stands as a direct result of the Company’s strategy to accelerate cash generation and maintain disciplined financial management through the efficient utilization of resources and capital allocation toward high-return opportunities.
Furthermore, moving into the Mid Cap segment strengthens Telecom Egypt’s appeal as an investment opportunity, enabling it to leverage inflows from index-tracking international funds. This change may support trading volumes, the Company’s visibility, and its credibility among global institutional investors.
This advancement also elevates the standing of the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) within the global capital markets landscape. It highlights the EGX’s ongoing advisory and guidance services for listed companies, as well as its continuous commitment to enhancing their competitiveness and strengthening their positioning in global indices.
The FTSE Russell Emerging Markets Index currently includes only three Egyptian companies, including Telecom Egypt. As one of the world's premier index providers, FTSE Russell tracks large- and mid-cap stocks across global emerging markets, serving as a critical benchmark for major investment funds and institutions to direct portfolio allocation. Inclusion is subject to a strict set of requirements, including market capitalization, liquidity, trading volumes, and free-float standards.
Telecom Egypt (WE), in collaboration with the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA) and Huawei, has successfully executed Egypt and Africa's first mobile service trial on the 6GHz (U6GHz) frequency band.
This trial aligns with Telecom Egypt's strategy of investing in cutting-edge technologies and maximizing the benefits of technological advancements that enhance customer experience and provide them with the highest level of services that meet their evolving needs.
This milestone reinforces Telecom Egypt's market leadership and proactive strategy to prepare for next-generation communications networks. The use of the 6GHz frequency band represents a significant opportunity to enhance mobile network capabilities by increasing network capacity and supporting data transfer speeds, enabling the operator to absorb surging data traffic and deliver higher-speed, ultra-efficient connectivity to its customers.
The trial involved operating the first mobile station using the 6GHz frequency band and establishing the first data connection through this band. The trial successfully achieved data transfer speeds of up to 1.7 Gbps per user.
H1 2026 Key Highlights
- Total revenue increased by 17% YoY, reaching EGP 59.2bn, driven by a 26% increase in Data revenue, followed by International Incoming Calls revenue up 32% YoY.
- Customer base increased YoY across Fixed Broadband, Fixed Voice, and Mobile by 9%, 6%, and 4%, respectively.
- EBITDA increased by 20% YoY, reaching EGP 26.4bn, with a margin of 45%.
- Net profit rose to EGP 15.4bn, marking a 47% YoY increment and a 26% net profit margin vs 21% in H1 2025.
- In-service CapEx reported EGP 4.9bn (8% of sales), while Cash CapEx (including license) reported EGP 18.6bn.
- Net debt/EBITDA (annualized) improved to 1.2x compared to 1.6x in H1 2025.
- FCFF reached EGP 10.0bn, implying a FCFF/EBITDA ratio of 38%.
“Telecom Egypt built on its resilience earlier in the year, delivering broad-based growth and stronger profitability in the first half of 2026. Our momentum this period underscores our ability to drive digital service expansion while mitigating the impact of broader regional and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Revenue grew 17% year-over-year to EGP 59.2 bn, driven by 26% growth in Data revenue and 32% growth in International Incoming Calls revenue. This reflects strong momentum across both our Retail and Wholesale businesses and supports the sustainability of our performance. Data growth reflected continued retail customer expansion and the initial benefits of the NTRA-approved tariff adjustments, while International Incoming Calls revenue benefitted from an 18% increase in traffic, forex gains, and sustained connectivity demand.
The strength of our operational performance is translating into a significant step-up in earnings and substantially higher net profitability.
EBITDA grew 20% to EGP 26.4 bn, with the margin reaching 45%. This reflected strong revenue growth, continued operational efficiency, and disciplined cost management despite challenging market conditions.
Reported net profit rose 47% from EGP 10.5 bn to EGP 15.4 bn, delivering a 26% net margin, up from 21% in H1 2025This performance reflects the continued progress of our core business and our ability to convert growth into higher earnings, despite the prevailing economic headwinds and the reported FX losses arising from broader foreign exchange movements.
Cash flow and leverage also improved during the period. FCFF reached EGP 10.0 bn, equivalent to 38% of EBITDA, while net debt to annualized EBITDA declined to 1.2x from 1.6x in the prior-year period, as we remain firmly focused and on track to deliver on our commitments.
Overall, underlying performance remained strong, while the stronger momentum seen in Q2 gives us greater confidence in our financial and operational outlook for the second half of the year.
Looking ahead, we will focus on sustaining this momentum and allocating capital carefully amid ongoing volatility. Beyond our traditional business, digital infrastructure remains an important opportunity with our wholly owned data center subsidiary providing a platform to serve growing enterprise and regional demand. We will continue to build beyond connectivity, pursue new digital opportunities and remain focused on disciplined execution, a strong balance sheet and long-term shareholder value.”
Engineer Tamer El-Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt, witnessed the closing ceremony for academic activities and Capstone Projects for students of WE Applied Technology Schools, "WE Shine". Held at Nile University, the event celebrated the students' success stories throughout the 2025–2026 academic year and recognized outstanding students for their academic excellence and technical skills.
These outstanding achievements showcased during the event, highlighted the pivotal role played by WE Applied Technology Schools —under the auspices of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) and in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Technical Education. The schools present a successful model that integrates academic study with practical training, offering students a genuine opportunity to acquire the experience and skills necessary for professional and academic excellence. Furthermore, they underscored Telecom Egypt’s firm belief in the importance of supporting applied technology education and contributing to the development of a new generation equipped with knowledge, skills, and innovative capabilities, aligned with labor market needs and Egypt's digital transformation across various sectors.
Throughout the 2025–2026 academic year, the Capstone Projects underwent an intensive development and evaluation journey. Students were divided into working groups under the supervision of specialized school engineers. Students submitted over 500 projects, which were presented to judging panels comprising university professors, engineers, and specialized experts. At the end of the evaluation phase, the top 90 projects were selected. Galaxy Development, one of the academic partners of WE Applied Technology Schools, managed and organized the closing ceremony and all stages of the competition. Working in coordination with various entities and training institutions, the company delivered activities and programs designed to develop students' skills and refining their technical capabilities, as well as to evaluate projects and select the top 15 for the final exhibition. Ultimately, the six best projects were chosen to win the top places across all schools in the country's governorates.
'WE Shine' event is a practical reflection of Telecom Egypt's vision of investing in human resources development and building a new generation of digital talent capable of leading the future of the digital economy. The outstanding innovative projects showcased today as part of the Capstone Program demonstrate the students' advanced academic achievements and practical competencies. They also confirm the success of WE Applied Technology Schools in delivering a modern educational model that aligns with the evolving needs of both local and international labor markets while preparing highly qualified cadres equipped with the knowledge and skills required to drive Egypt's digital transformation."
“We believe that investing in education is an investment in the nation’s future. From this standpoint, we continue to develop this educational model in collaboration with our partners, foremost among them (MCIT) to ensure the graduation of generations of creative minds and innovators capable of supporting Egypt’s competitiveness, effectively contributing to achieving the goals of the Digital Egypt strategy, and building a knowledge- and innovation-based economy,” he added.
"WE Shine event underscores the importance of collaborative efforts among the Ministry of Education and Technical Education, (MCIT), and all national institutions and development partners. These efforts aim to prepare technical cadres equipped with the digital and innovative skills required for the future, thereby enhancing the competitiveness of the Egyptian economy."
"Celebrating students' achievements in WE Shine 2026 is not merely an acknowledgment of outstanding performance; it is also a testament to the success of the state's vision for transforming technical and technological education into an ecosystem that fosters innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship. This contributes to preparing qualified national cadres capable of meeting labor market demands and keeping pace with the Fourth Industrial Revolution," he added.
Telecom Egypt (WE), Egypt’s first integrated Telecom operator, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Grova Developments, the real estate arm of Hassan Allam Holding Group. This strategic partnership aims deliver advanced telecommunications infrastructure and smart city solutions for Grova Developments, aligning with Telecom Egypt's strategy to bolster the digital infrastructure of new urban communities and enhance their readiness for digital transformation.
The agreement was signed by Mr. Mohamed El-Touny, Vice President and Chief Consumer Officer of Telecom Egypt, and Mr. Sherif Mohamed Sadeq, CEO of Grova Developments. The signing ceremony took place in the presence of Engineer Hassan Allam, Chairman and CEO of Hassan Allam Holding, and Engineer Tamer El-Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt.
Under the agreement, Telecom Egypt will take on the establishment and development of the project's entire telecommunications network infrastructure, including advanced Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) technology and activation of XGPON technology to guarantee ultra-high-speed internet services, in addition to offering Triple Play solutions that include high-speed internet, landline telephone, and IPTV digital television services for end users. Telecom Egypt will also provide the latest value-added digital amenities, such as Home Automation, Community Mobile App, Public Wi-Fi, and other cutting-edge digital technologies.
Sayed, "This partnership marks a significant milestone in Telecom Egypt's mission to drive digital transformation and build smart infrastructure for Egypt's modern urban communities. We are proud to collaborate with Grova Developments, a subsidiary of the prestigious Hassan Allam Group. We remain committed to leveraging our extensive expertise and investing heavily in Egypt's largest fiber-optic network to deliver tangible value to our real estate partners and equip their developments with future-ready smart city solutions."
For his part, Sherif Sadeq, CEO of Grova Developments, said "Our partnership with Telecom Egypt reflects our core vision of building sustainable, integrated communities that offer long-term value for future generations. We are keen on providing all the elements that contribute to delivering a complete living experience, including advanced digital infrastructure, which has become an essential part of modern lifestyles. This collaboration leverages Hassan Allam Holding Group's 90-year legacy of executing complex projects and vital infrastructure, allowing us to deliver an unparalleled lifestyle experience that blends innovation with premium quality."
Remarked: "This agreement underscores Telecom Egypt’s dedication to equipping premier real estate projects with industry-leading telecommunications solutions. By partnering with Grova Developments, we aim to deliver a seamless, high-quality digital experience. Leveraging advanced fiber-optic technologies and robust smart solutions, we will ensure peak network efficiency and reliability, successfully meeting the evolving demands of today's digital lifestyle."
Telecom Egypt (WE), first integrated telecom operator in Egypt, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with VIE Communities for Investments and Development. Under this strategic partnership, Telecom Egypt will design and deploy state-of-the-art digital infrastructure and smart services for all VIE Communities’ projects while supporting the digital infrastructure of new urban communities and enhancing their readiness for digital transformation. The agreement was signed by Mr. Mohamed El-Touny, Vice President & Chief Consumer Officer at Telecom Egypt, and Dr. Haitham Samir, CEO of VIE Communities.
Under the agreement, Telecom Egypt WE will implement a robust Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) network to ensure the delivery of high-efficiency, ultra-fast internet connectivity services. These efforts will directly enhance customer experience and improve service efficiency.
The partnership reflects the shared commitment of both parties to implementing the highest standards of quality and innovation, and to developing an integrated digital infrastructure that keeps pace with the rapid evolution of the telecommunications and information technology sector. This will support the transition toward smart developments and strengthen the projects’ readiness to meet future technological demands.
At Telecom Egypt said, "Telecom Egypt remains committed to reinforcing its leading role in driving national digital transformation and pioneering infrastructure development across diverse sectors through innovative technology solutions that contribute to building more connected and sustainable communities. With our extensive expertise in telecommunications and digital infrastructure, we are well positioned to deliver tangible value to our partners. This agreement marks a significant milestone in supporting smart real estate ventures, and we look forward to transforming VIE Communities' projects into benchmarks for modern, sustainably connected communities built on advanced digital infrastructure that delivers innovative services and an exceptional customer experience."
“At VIE Communities, we believe that advanced digital infrastructure is now a fundamental cornerstone of successful, modern real estate development. Therefore, we are committed to collaborating with organizations that possess the expertise and capabilities required to deliver advanced solutions that meet future demands. Our strategic partnership with Telecom Egypt represents a pivotal step in evolving our flagship 'Vie Collective' project, enhancing the value we offer to our customers and providing an integrated living experience powered by the latest technologies and smart services. This partnership is part of our long-term vision to build integrated and sustainable communities that meet the aspirations of the new generation of customers and provide a more connected and innovative living environment, he added.
In a major stride toward accelerating Egypt’s digital economy and fostering tech entrepreneurship, Telecom Egypt (WE), the National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA), and the Arab Academy for Science, Technology, and Maritime Transport (AASTMT) have officially inaugurated a new Cybersecurity Innovation Lab at the AASTMT Smart Village campus.
The facility launches under the umbrella of the "WE Innovate Star" program, a flagship Telecom Egypt initiative designed to build an end-to-end ecosystem for applied innovation. The lab will bridge the gap between academic research and practical application, offering students, researchers, and startups an advanced environment to develop and test market-ready solutions in cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and modern technology. It also falls under Telecom Egypt's strategy to establish a network of specialized and diverse innovation labs covering different stages of the innovation journey. This starts from supporting scientific research and developing ideas into minimum viable products (MVPs), to developing products and testing them in real operating environments, and accelerating the readiness of startups for growth and expansion.
These labs provide a comprehensive environment for students, researchers, entrepreneurs, and startups to develop innovative solutions and technologies that meet market needs, support digital transformation efforts, and strengthen Egypt's position as a regional hub for innovation and technology.
During the inauguration, Engineer Tamer El-Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO of Telecom Egypt, and Professor Dr. Ismail Abdel Ghaffar, President of AASTMT, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to solidify the operational framework of the lab and provide a supportive environment for innovation through specialized training programs, technical guidance, and practical workshops, in addition to enhancing the integration between academic and research expertise on one hand, and practical and technological expertise on the other.
"We take pride in our strategic partnership with Telecom Egypt, which reflects a true integration between academic excellence and practical expertise. The lab provides our researchers and students with a high-tech platform to sharpen their skills, preparing a new generation to lead Egypt’s digital future."
The high-profile inauguration was attended by key leaders across the ICT and academic sectors, including, Engineer Tamer El-Mahdy, Managing Director and CEO, Telecom Egypt, Engineer Walid Zakaria, Vice President for Cybersecurity Affairs, NTRA. Engineer Walaa Salah El-Din, Advisor to the CEO for Innovation and Cybersecurity, Telecom Egypt, Dr. Aliaa El-Gazzar, Dean of the Faculty of Computers and Information Technology, AASTMT, representatives from AGX Consultant (the implementing partner of the WE Innovate Star program) alongside participating tech teams and entrepreneurs.
The Cybersecurity Innovation Lab is considered one of the main components of the innovation system, aiming to create a complete path to support innovation, starting from scientific research and idea development, going through building prototypes and proof of concept, and reaching product development and testing in real operational environments, all while accelerating the growth of startups. Through this collaborative ecosystem, Telecom Egypt and its partners continue to solidify Egypt’s position as the premier regional hub for technological innovation and digital transformation.
Telecom Egypt (WE), in collaboration with Huawei, announced today the launch of a new Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) service, powered by Huawei’s advanced solutions. The new technology marks a major milestone in the evolution of home broadband services in Egypt, delivering customers an ultra-fast, stable, and seamless connectivity experience, while enhancing wireless network coverage across every corner of the home.
Huawei’s FTTR technology represents a new generation of in-home fiber optic networking solutions, purpose-built to overcome common connectivity challenges such asdead zones, inconsistent speeds, and network congestion resulting from the growing number of connected devices in large multi-room and multi-story homes, ultimately meeting the evolving needs and expectations of customers. In addition, the FTTR service serves as an ideal solution for smart homes, gaming enthusiasts, and users who rely heavily on technology for work and daily activities, all of whom require ultra-fast internet connectivity with minimal latency to ensure optimal performance.
Designed to meet the evolving demands of next-generation entertainment and digital lifestyles, the service delivers a future-ready infrastructure capable of supporting the growing reliance on digital services and smart home applications. It efficiently enables high-speed online gaming, remote work and learning, as well as ultra-high-definition video streaming in resolutions of up to 4K and 8K. The solution is also distinguished by its ability to support a large number of simultaneously connected devices without compromising network reliability, stability, or overall performance efficiency.
The newly launched solution also offers fast and simplified deployment, allowing customers to benefit from quick installation with minimal disruption inside the home. Through intelligent network management and advanced optical technologies, the fiber cables could be extended in the existing home ducts or through the newly introduced transparent sticky fiber cables that ensures connectivity without affecting home decorations.
“The launch of FTTR service today marks a defining milestone in our journey toward shaping the future of digital services in Egypt, and a strong reaffirmation of our commitment to delivering innovative solutions that consistently exceed our customers’ expectations. We are not simply enhancing internet speeds; we are building a smart, fully integrated in-home digital infrastructure that empowers households to fully unlock the potential of the latest global technologies.”
He added: “Launching the FTTR in collaboration with Huawei Egypt reflects the strength of our strategic partnership, enabling us to accelerate the introduction of advanced technologies into the Egyptian market in a way that directly elevates the customer experience for individuals and SMEs alike. It delivers a more resilient, efficient, and stable infrastructure, designed to keep pace with the rapidly growing demand for digital services.”
“Our partnership with Telecom Egypt (WE) in launching FTTR service represents a strategic milestone that reflects our shared commitment to accelerating Egypt’s digital transformation in line with Egypt Vision 2030, while elevating telecommunications infrastructure standards to global levels.”
He added: “Since beginning our journey in Egypt more than a quarter of a century ago, Huawei has remained committed to its global vision of building a fully connected and intelligent world. The importance of this technology extends beyond enhancing the home connectivity experience; it also lays the foundation for advanced connectivity solutions that support both households and SMEs. By delivering ultra-high speeds, greater stability, and a more efficient and reliable user experience, it is well positioned to meet future demands and support the continued growth of Egypt’s digital economy.”
To make adoption easier for interested customers, Telecom Egypt (WE ) announced the launch of its FTTR service, supported by round-the-clock technical assistance and professional installation carried out by a dedicated team of trained technicians, ensuring a smooth and seamless customer experience from activation to setup.
Q1 2026 Key Highlights
- Total revenue grew 14% YoY to EGP 28.2bn, led by Total Data revenue (+23% YoY), contributing 69% of total revenue growth, International Incoming Calls revenue (+27% YoY), and Domestic Infrastructure Services revenue (+18% YoY).
- Customer base growth remained positive across Mobile, Fixed Broadband, and Fixed Voice, rising 7%, 8%, and 7% YoY, respectively.
- EBITDA rose 17% YoY to EGP 12.6bn, with the EBITDA margin reaching 45%, supported by healthy organic growth.
- Net profit reached EGP 3.6bn, with a 13% net margin. Operational performance remained healthy, with the YoY movement driven mainly by higher non-cash FX losses of EGP 5.3bn and a 15% increase in D&A, partly offset by a 25% reduction in interest expense. On an adjusted basis, excluding non-cash FX losses, net profit would have reached c. EGP 5.9bn, up nearly 27% YoY.
- In-service Capex amounted to EGP 1.3bn, representing 5% of sales, while Cash Capex (including license) reached EGP 8.8bn, representing 31% of sales.
- Net debt/EBITDA stood at 1.3x at period-end, improving from 1.6x in Q1 25, supported by solid EBITDA growth and disciplined leverage management leading to a reduction in net debt of EGP 8bn.
- FCFF rose to EGP 6.4bn up from EGP 3.5bn YoY, driven by stronger cash generation and improved working capital and capex efficiency.
Q1 2026 unfolded against an unusually complex operating environment, with heightened regional geopolitical tensions adding volatility even as Egypt's macroeconomic stabilization continued following the March 2024 FX liberalization. Against this backdrop, Telecom Egypt delivered a resilient performance, underpinned by the defensive nature of connectivity demand, our diversified revenue base, and the natural hedge provided by our USD-linked international wholesale revenues.
Revenue grew 14% YoY to EGP 28.2 billion, and EBITDA rose 17% to EGP 12.6 billion at a healthy 45% margin. Net profit was EGP 3.6 billion, with a 13% net margin. While the reported result absorbed a EGP 5.3 billion non-cash FX loss linked to the revaluation of foreign-currency liabilities, our operations remained healthy: excluding this non-cash effect, net profit would have reached c. EGP 5.9 billion, up nearly 27% YoY.
Commercial momentum stayed strong across all segments, with our Mobile, Data, and Fixed subscriber bases growing 7%, 8%, and 7% YoY, respectively. This rests on the quality of our network: in February 2026, independent analytics firm Opensignal recognized WE as Egypt's Best Network, with eight awards, including seven outright wins across categories such as Download Speed Experience, Reliability Experience and Consistent Quality.
Following the recent reorganization of our retail structure, we are sharpening our focus on the Enterprise segment, expanding tailored solutions for SME and SOHO customers and scaling our fixed-mobile convergence (FMC) and digital services.
We remain focused on upgrading and strengthening the resilience of our infrastructure, while continuing to scale and capitalize on these USD-generating revenue streams. Our international cables and wholesale business continued to play a critical role in global connectivity. Egypt's strategic position — anchoring over 90% of data traffic between Europe, Asia, and Africa — together with rising demand for secure, diversified routing in the current geopolitical environment, has further reinforced the structural relevance of our infrastructure.
We continued to advance our long-term network roadmap, drawing on the 2026–2030 National Spectrum Strategy to expand capacity and scale next-generation services, including our ongoing 5G rollout. We continued to manage capital prudently during the quarter, with Cash Capex (including license) of EGP 8.8 billion (approximately 31% of sales) compared with EGP 6.8 billion on the same basis in Q1 2025. Meanwhile FCFF strengthened to EGP 6.4 billion versus EGP 3.5 billion in Q1 2025. FAQ
1. What is eKYC?
eKYC is a digital process that verifies your identity securely using your mobile phone—without needing to visit the store or submit physical documents.
2. When is eKYC required?
eKYC is required to:
Activate new services
Complete certain transactions
Ensure your account is legally compliant
3. Is eKYC mandatory?
Yes, eKYC is required to:
Comply with NTRA and protect customer rights
Prevent fraud, identity theft, and misuse of telecom services
Enable faster, safer, and fully digital service activation
4. What information will be collected during eKYC?
We may collect:
Your national ID details
A live photo (selfie) for face matching
Basic personal information required for verification
All data is handled securely
5. How does the eKYC verification work?
The process typically includes:
Entering your personal details
Capturing your ID information
Taking a live selfie
Matching your face with your ID using secure technology
6. Is my data safe?
Yes. Your data is:
Encrypted and securely processed
Used only for verification purposes
Protected under strict confidentiality and data privacy regulations
7. How long does the eKYC process take?
The process usually takes a few minutes, and verification is completed almost instantly in most cases.
8. What happens if my verification fails?
If verification fails:
You may be asked to retry the process (up to 3 trials)
Ensure good lighting and clear image capture
Contact customer support if the issue persists
9. Do I need a SIM card during verification?
Yes, Verification is typically linked to your mobile line, unless otherwise specified under approved conditions.
10. Can I use eKYC services at any time?
eKYC services are available:
24/7 (all day, every day) for your convenience
11. What are the benefits of using eKYC?
No need to visit a store
Faster service activation
More secure identity verification
Seamless digital experience
12. What if I face technical issues during eKYC?
If you experience issues:
Try again after a few minutes
Contact customer support if the problem continues
If you choose not to complete it, some services may not be available.

title: e-SIM
text:
e-SIM
What is e-SIM technology?
An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a digital version of a traditional SIM card that is built directly into a device, unlike the physical SIM card. It allows devices to connect to mobile networks using software-based profiles that can be remotely provisioned and managed. This technology enables greater flexibility, convenience, and security for mobile connectivity.
How to activate the e-SIM?

- Purchase the eSIM, pay the required fees, and you will receive a QR code to activate the service.
- Ensure your phone is connected to Wi-Fi.
- Scan the QR code to download the line profile and network definitions on the eSIM.
- To activate the line, contact our call center “111” for user data validation, then line activation.
Steps to Convert a Physical SIM to an eSIM Using My WE App
- Ensure that your device supports eSIM technology.
- Make sure you are connected to mobile internet using the SIM you want to replace.
- Click on "Switch to eSIM" in the app (available below "More" or "New from WE" on the Home page).
- Confirm your email and accept the terms and conditions.
- A verification code will be sent to the SIM you are replacing.
- Take photos of your national ID (front and back).
- Enter your maternal grandfather's name in Arabic.
- The eSIM price will be displayed, and you can proceed with online payment.
- Before payment, ensure you are connected to Wi-Fi, as you will switch to it. After payment, your physical SIM will be deactivated.
- A QR code valid for 5 days will be sent to you after payment.
- Scan the QR code and follow the steps to download the eSIM profile.

title: Mobile Number Portability
text:
Mobile Number Portability
- How to change to WE network?
- Bring your personal identification and verify the data in the nearest WE store
- National ID must be valid and not damaged
- You may receive your unpaid bills of your previous operator/s within your first 60 days of subscription with WE
- Confirm the transfer request when the phone call is received
- Terminate all financial receivables in the donor mobile company before transferring
- What are the service fees?
- MNP service for free and customer get the new Sim card for free from WE stores.
- How long does it take to fulfill the porting in?
- 24 working hours for the activation after approval from the other operator to transfer.
- Where can I create an MNP request?
- Through any of WE main stores
- Can the application be rejected by the other company? What should I do if that happens?
- Yes, the application could be rejected and you should submit complaint to 155 from the same number if the reason is not valid.
- Can I port in more than one line at the same time?
- No, you can’t port in more than one line at the same time.
- What are the terms and conditions?
- You can’t revert to another operator before 4 months of service at the new operator
- You must ensure that all your data is complete and correct before making the porting in request.
- You can’t port out of WE network before 4 months
- Any port in request may be canceled within maximum 24 working hours from the application submission time, and the request cannot be cancelled if line is activated.
- No remaining balance, features or services will be transferred to you from the mobile network company you wish to transfer from
- Is it required to bring my account number, SIM serial number, or the transferring company's code?
- It is absolutely not required to bring the account number, SIM serial number, or the transferring company's code when submitting the transfer request.
